title: Minimum Guaranteed Serve Rate and Graceful Degradation Prioritization Framework
creator: Logan Rivera
description: Define a minimum guaranteed serve-rate (tokens/sec or requests/sec depending on contract) and an ordered, auditable graceful-degradation policy that determines which traffic classes are demoted during capacity shortfalls. Produce contract wording and measurement primitives that map runtime telemetry to credit calculations.
background: Enterprise customers require clearer semantics for what we guarantee during sustained load and partial failures. Existing artifacts focus on credit calculations and error budgets; this ticket synthesizes a defendable minimum-serve definition plus a prioritization framework for graceful degradation so customers and account teams can reason about application-level impact.
scope:
- Define a min-serve metric (quantile-driven) and measurement window
- Specify prioritization tiers and demotion rules (route-level, token-class, model-variant)
- Draft contract language for inclusion in Dedicated agreements
- Add telemetry and alerts needed to operationalize measurement
- Provide rollout and customer communication plan
out_of_scope:
- Implementation of autoscaler code changes (ENG tickets will track)
- Legal negotiation of final SLA text (Legal will iterate on drafts)
- Per-customer bespoke prioritization configs (handled as custom work)
acceptance_criteria:
- Documented min-serve metric definition with a worked example (tokens/min and requests/min)
- Prioritization ladder defined with deterministic demotion rules and example failure scenarios
- Draft contract clause that legal accepts as starting point
- Runbook entries for measuring and computing credits produced
- End-to-end playbook validated in tabletop with SRE and Sales
technical_considerations:
- Measurement must be computable from existing serving runtime telemetry (per-shard QPS, token emit rate, drop counts)
- Need mapping from request-level attributes to priority tiers (API key tags, route metadata)
- Autoscaler interaction: must detect degraded window and not thrash when scaling slowly
- KV cache and batching can mask client-level degradation—ensure measurement accounts for effective throughput
- Privacy: measurement will not include PII; only aggregated usage metrics
contract_language_snippet: During any 1-hour measurement window, Redwood guarantees a Minimum Guaranteed Serve Rate (MGSR) equal to X tokens/min (or Y requests/min) for the contracted capacity tier. If the observed MGSR falls below the contracted threshold for more than Z minutes within the measurement window, Redwood will compute Service Credits proportional to the deviation per the credit schedule. Redwood may apply prioritized degradation in the event of sustained capacity pressure; prioritization tiers and demotion rules are specified in Appendix A of this agreement.
metrics_and_alerting:
- MGSR (tokens/min) computed per-AZ and aggregated for customer
- Degradation window counter (minutes below threshold)
- Priority-demotion events log (route, time, reason)
- Alert: >5 minutes continuous MGSR deficit -> Pager to SRE on-call
- Dashboard: Customer MGSR heatmap, per-route percent of served requests
rollout_plan:
1) Align on definitions with SRE and Eng (week 1)
2) Add telemetry hooks and dashboard mocks (week 2)
3) Legal review draft contract language and iterate (week 3)
4) Tabletop run with Sales/Solution Eng for 2 pilot customers (week 4)
5) Ship Appendix A and measurement tooling in release dedicated-2025.12
